Table 2 gives means (SD), average/good creative tendency respectively: unaided 3.44 (0.83)/3.44 (0.69); Internet-assisted 3.56 (0.74)/3.59 (0.89); GenAI-assisted 3.37 (1.23)/3.58 (1.00). Section 4.1 reports no significant method main effect (p > 0.05), with Greenhouse-Geisser-corrected degrees of freedom used; an exact F statistic and exact p-value are not supplied. corrections.source_says: The 41-person count, the three printed F statistics and the direction of the scored-outcome findings are supported, including the originality comparison in Figure 4. Qualify the broad claim that creativity support was higher with GenAI: Section 4.2 reports higher usability, exploration and immersion versus unaided ideation, but result worth effort favored Internet-assisted over GenAI-assisted (p = 0.040), and expressiveness and enjoyment had no significant overall method effects. A revised finding should also acknowledge the null elaboration result and give pp. 9-10 as the locator for the support claims.

corrections.form_value: 41 second-year product-design students at Quzhou University each did three 10-minute chair-design ideation tasks in a lab: unaided, Internet-assisted (Baidu Images), and GenAI-assisted (Doubao text-to-image). Task order was counterbalanced by a systematic rotation schedule, and creative tendency (average vs. good) was a between-subjects factor. Three design experts rated the sketches for flexibility, originality, and elaboration on 5-point scales, fluency was the count of distinct ideas, and participants self-reported perceived creativity support.
corrections.source_says: The paper explicitly identifies the sample as product-design students from a single Chinese university. Quzhou University is named as the ethics-approving institution and an author affiliation, but the participant passage does not explicitly identify it as the recruitment institution. Replace the unqualified recruitment claim at Quzhou University with from a single Chinese university, or label the institution as an inference rather than a reported fact.
corrections.quote: Third, the use of novice product design students from a single Chinese university limits generalizability.
corrections.locator: p. 1, author affiliations; p. 5, Section 3.1 Participants; p. 14, Section 5.5; p. 15, Ethics statement

confirmed: Version checked: the 18-page journal version of record by Huan Lin and Letian Xie, Frontiers in Psychology 17:1839565, published 30 June 2026; the form correctly identifies the title, authors, date and version (p. 1; PDF page count). The checker read the complete markdown in chunks and extracted PDF text on all pages, with direct inspection of Figures 2, 4 and 5.

The paper reports one 3 x 2 mixed experiment: ideation method is within-person and measured creative tendency is between-person; every student performs all methods (p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, Section 3.3). Random assignment and preregistration are not stated (pp. 4-6, Methods).

The sample is 41 second-year product-design students, with 21 average and 20 good creative-tendency participants; mean age = 19.5 years, SD = 1.27 (p. 5, Section 3.1). The Results explicitly report 41 datasets analyzed (p. 8, Section 4).

The 41 participants are the same people across conditions, not separate arm samples or counts of sketches or ratings; keep randomized counts null, and do not add the repeated condition counts. No participant exclusions or total sketch/rating counts are stated (pp. 5-8, Sections 3.1-4).

The size exclusion is correct: 41 people analyzed is below the codebook threshold of 50; creativity is scored on produced output, so criterion 3 is met (p. 8, Section 4; p. 7, Table 1 and Section 3.4; creativity-codebook.md, Section 3).

Each chair-design condition lasts 10 minutes, and the GenAI condition follows a 5-minute prompt tutorial. Doubao supplies text-to-image inspiration that students refine or extend through freehand sketching; Baidu Images is the Internet aid (pp. 5-6, Sections 3.2-3.3).

Three blinded design experts evaluate output; fluency counts distinct ideas, while flexibility, originality and elaboration use 5-point ratings. The perceived-support measures are separate self-reports, not output scores (pp. 5-7, Sections 3.2-3.4 and Table 1).

Originality numbers match: unaided average/good 3.18 (0.87)/3.29 (0.67), GenAI average/good 2.89 (0.99)/2.98 (0.60); F(2,38) = 10.170, p < 0.001, partial eta squared = 0.349. Internet exceeds unaided at p = 0.036 and GenAI at p < 0.001 (p. 8, Table 2 and Section 4.1).

Fluency numbers match: unaided average/good 2.53 (1.02)/3.45 (2.09), GenAI average/good 1.89 (0.81)/2.45 (1.34); F(2,38) = 5.583, p = 0.002, partial eta squared = 0.289. Unaided exceeds GenAI at p = 0.002 (p. 8, Table 2 and Section 4.1).

Flexibility numbers match: unaided average/good 3.35 (0.77)/3.52 (0.88), GenAI average/good 2.77 (0.73)/3.08 (0.68); F(2,38) = 12.724, p < 0.001, partial eta squared = 0.401. Unaided exceeds GenAI at p < 0.001 (p. 8, Table 2 and Section 4.1).

The F values in the one-line finding are copied correctly and describe omnibus method effects. All numeric values above are retained as printed; no standardized mean difference or unreported exact p-value was computed (p. 8, Section 4.1).

The paper is an original experiment, not a synthesis: the literature-review section supplies background, and there are no pooled study counts, estimates or intervals to extract (p. 1, article type; pp. 4-10, Methods and Results).

No appendix or supplement is included or referred to in the source; the final pages contain references. Raw data are promised by the authors, with no public data or code URL stated (p. 15, Data availability statement; pp. 16-18, References).

The authors declare no commercial or financial relationships constituting a conflict, while the raters include two experts with experience in a Chinese furniture enterprise (p. 15, Conflict of interest; p. 7, Section 3.4). No AI-vendor involvement is stated.

Source inconsistency relevant to the support summary: Figure 5 shows a three-star exploration bracket for GenAI versus Internet, whereas Section 4.2 reports p > 0.05; its Internet-versus-unaided exploration bracket has three stars although the prose gives p = 0.004. Figure 5 also marks Internet-versus-unaided immersion with two stars while the prose says Internet differs from neither alternative (p. 10, Figure 5 and Section 4.2). These discrepancies are unresolved.
summary: The paper reports 41 analyzed students in a systematically counterbalanced study without documented random assignment, so lab_rct and context_class none need correction. The recorded numbers match the PDF, but the form omits elaboration, active-comparator results and figure evidence, overgeneralizes perceived creativity support, and needs sampling-detail corrections.
